sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马尔斯。

sentences.en: It's safe to say that Woods Hole is exactly what you picture when you think of a town on Cape Cod.
sentences.zh: 可以说，伍兹霍尔正是你脑海中对科德角小镇的典型想象。

sentences.en: Old houses covered in wood shingles.
sentences.zh: 古老的房屋挂满了木质瓦片。

sentences.en: There are sailboats, oceanside restaurants.
sentences.zh: 到处都是帆船和海滨餐厅。

sentences.en: Wealthy vacationers in the summertime.
sentences.zh: 夏天有富裕的度假客。

sentences.en: Super traditional, super east coaSt.
sentences.zh: 超级传统，超级东海岸。

sentences.en: But just up the hill from the tiny downtown, there's this huge dome.
sentences.zh: 但在繁华小镇中心旁的小山坡上，有一座巨大的穹顶建筑。

sentences.en: It looks like a three-story tall golf ball.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像一个三层楼高的巨型高尔夫球。

sentences.en: It's this crazy-looking white building, totally out of place next to the old colonial houses.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋看起来非常疯狂的白色建筑，夹在古老的殖民风格房屋旁，显得格格不入。

sentences.en: So reporter Katie Clarkson went to check it out.
sentences.zh: 于是记者凯蒂·克拉克森前去一探究竟。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 哈喽。

sentences.en: Katie brought some friends, too.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂还带了几个朋友。

sentences.en: The back door was unlocked.
sentences.zh: 后门没有锁。

sentences.en: It's not like anything you've ever seen before.
sentences.zh: 这跟你以前见过的任何东西都不同。

sentences.en: Inside, it smells musty.
sentences.zh: 里面有一股霉味。

sentences.en: It's creepy.
sentences.zh: 让人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: Look at this old wallpaper.
sentences.zh: 看这古老的壁纸。

sentences.en: There's a wall made entirely out of these interlocking, triangle-shaped windows.
sentences.zh: 有一面墙完全是由这种互锁的三角形窗户组成的。

sentences.en: They cast a web of shadows on the floor.
sentences.zh: 它们在地板上投下一网状的阴影。

sentences.en: There's an old kitchen.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个老旧的厨房。

sentences.en: It looks like it might have been part of a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 看起来它以前可能是餐厅的一部分。

sentences.en: You found some?
sentences.zh: 你们找到了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a whole pile of old salt and pepper.
sentences.zh: 找到了，这里有一大堆旧盐和胡椒粉。

sentences.en: Oh, great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: When we left, I needed to know more.
sentences.zh: 当我们离开时，我迫切想了解更多。

sentences.en: What Katie found was a geodesic dome, designed and built by the late Buckminster Fuller.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂发现的是一座测地穹顶建筑，由已故的巴克敏斯特·富勒设计和建造。

sentences.en: Don't feel bad if you've never heard of Bucky.
sentences.zh: 如果你从未听说过巴基，也不用感到不好意思。

sentences.en: He did go by Bucky, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他确实叫巴基。

sentences.en: He was a big deal back in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 他在60年代可是个大人物。

sentences.en: A drawing of Bucky's head, made to look like one of his domes, was on the cover of Time magazine in 1964.
sentences.zh: 1964年，《时代》杂志的封面印着一幅巴基的头像画，被设计成他穹顶建筑的模样。

sentences.en: There's a Bucky Fuller postage stamp.
sentences.zh: 还有一张巴基·富勒的纪念邮票。

sentences.en: He was even given the country's highest civilian honor, a Presidential Medal of Freedom.
sentences.zh: 他甚至被授予了该国最高的平民荣誉——总统自由勋章。

sentences.en: Bucky Fuller is also responsible for the title of this radio show.
sentences.zh: 巴基·富勒也是这个广播节目名称的灵感来源。

sentences.en: He said, 99% of who you are is invisible and untouchable.
sentences.zh: 他说，你身上99%的部分是隐形且不可触及的。

sentences.en: And he discussed the 99% invisible activity that is coalescing to reshape our future.
sentences.zh: 他还讨论了正在汇聚并重塑我们未来的那99%的隐形活动。

sentences.en: He's a very quotable man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个满嘴金句的人。

sentences.en: Here he is from the film Buckminster Fuller, The Lost Interviews.
sentences.zh: 这是他在纪录片《巴克敏斯特·富勒：遗失的访谈》中的影像。

sentences.en: I think we ought to be looking into what needs to be done to do more with less,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该研究如何用更少的资源做更多的事，

sentences.en: so that you might sometimes do so much with so little you might be able to take care of everybody
sentences.zh: 这样有时你就能以极少的资源做出巨大的成就，从而照顾好每个人，

sentences.en: and make all of politics invalid.
sentences.zh: 并让所有的政治手段变得不再必要。

sentences.en: Jay Baldwin was one of Bucky's students.
sentences.zh: 杰伊·鲍德温是巴基的学生之一。

sentences.en: He just wanted people to use less stuff.
sentences.zh: 他只是希望人们少用点东西。

sentences.en: He said it was all going to run out.
sentences.zh: 他说这些资源终将耗尽。

sentences.en: We've got to think big and take care of everybody.
sentences.zh: 我们必须胸怀大局，照顾好每一个人。

sentences.en: He said as long as there's one person starving, you're going to have wars.
sentences.zh: 他说，只要还有一个在挨饿，就会一直有战争。

sentences.en: Fuller called himself a comprehensive, anticipatory design scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 富勒称自己为全面、前瞻性的设计科学家。

sentences.en: He wanted to invent things that would make human life sustainable on this planet.
sentences.zh: 他想要发明能让人类生命在这颗星球上实现可持续发展的物品。

sentences.en: Decades before anyone else was even thinking about green buildings.
sentences.zh: 这比其他人开始关注绿色建筑早了几十年。

sentences.en: And for that, people have called Bucky the Leonardo da Vinci of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，人们称巴基为20世纪的列奥纳多·达·芬奇。

sentences.en: Oh yes, they do that, but the Fuller Institute crew counters that Leonardo was the Bucky Fuller of medieval times.
sentences.zh: 哦对，人们确实这么叫，但富勒研究所的团队反驳说，列奥纳多其实是中世纪的巴基·富勒。

sentences.en: So here's the deal with the Woods Hole Dome.
sentences.zh: 这就是伍兹霍尔穹顶建筑的由来。

sentences.en: Bucky wanted to change the world, starting with buildings.
sentences.zh: 巴基想要改变世界，从建筑开始。

sentences.en: So he started making these weird structures, which he called geodesic domes.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始建造这些奇怪的结构，他称之为测地穹顶。

sentences.en: Geodesic refers to the geometry of curved surfaces.
sentences.zh: 测地指的是曲面的几何学。

sentences.en: The golf ball building in Woods Hole is actually the oldest of Bucky's domes that are still standing.
sentences.zh: 伍兹霍尔那个高尔夫球形状的建筑，其实是巴基现存最古老的穹顶建筑。

sentences.en: The structure of the geodesic dome is based on a lot of complicated math.
sentences.zh: 测地穹顶的结构基于大量复杂的数学原理。

sentences.en: But in short, it's built with a lot of triangles.
sentences.zh: 但简而言之，它是由许多三角形构建的。

sentences.en: A triangle is a very strong shape.
sentences.zh: 三角形是一种非常坚固的形状。

sentences.en: And a dome made out of triangles is extra strong.
sentences.zh: 由三角形构成的穹顶则异常坚固。

sentences.en: That meant that domes could be made of lighter and cheaper materials than normal buildings,
sentences.zh: 这意味着穹顶可以使用比普通建筑更轻、更便宜的材料，

sentences.en: like plastic and aluminum, instead of steel and concrete.
sentences.zh: 比如塑料和铝，而不是钢筋和混凝土。

sentences.en: Back in 1952, Bucky was just starting to build domes.
sentences.zh: 早在1952年，巴基才刚刚开始建造穹顶。

sentences.en: They caught the attention of an architect and aspiring restaurateur, a man named Gunner Peterson.
sentences.zh: 它们引起了一位建筑师兼有志成为餐馆老板的人的注意，他叫冈纳·彼得森。

sentences.en: And in the early 50s, 1953, he bought some property in Woods Hole and decided to build a hotel and a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 在50年代初，即1953年，他在伍兹霍尔买下了一些地产，决定建造一家酒店和一家餐厅。

sentences.en: Joel Peterson is Gunner's son.
sentences.zh: 乔尔·彼得森是冈纳的儿子。

sentences.en: He did make a deal with Bucky Fuller.
sentences.zh: 他确实和巴基·富勒做成了这笔交易。

sentences.en: I don't remember how Dad met him.
sentences.zh: 我不记得爸爸是怎么认识他的。

sentences.en: He, like, maybe called him up.
sentences.zh: 他，呃，可能给他打过电话。

sentences.en: I don't, you know, I mean, he tracked him down anyway.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，你知道的，我的意思是，总之他找到了他。

sentences.en: And Bucky and his wife came and lived at our house.
sentences.zh: 然后巴基和他的妻子搬来住在了我们家。

sentences.en: They decided they'd build the dome restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他们决定建造那家穹顶餐厅。

sentences.en: A geodesic dome has a way of standing out.
sentences.zh: 测地穹顶自带一种引人注目的特质。

sentences.en: But in Cape Cod, it really stands out.
sentences.zh: 但在科德角，它确实格外显眼。

sentences.en: And that upsets some people.
sentences.zh: 这让一些人很不高兴。

sentences.en: Well, it isn't a shingled Cape Cod cottage.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它可不是贴着木瓦的科德角小屋。

sentences.en: That's for darn sure.
sentences.zh: 那是千真万确的。

sentences.en: And the feeling is this is going to change life as we know it.
sentences.zh: 大家的感受是，这将会改变我们熟知的生活方式。

sentences.en: You know, we'll never be the same again.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们将再也回不到过去了。

sentences.en: You know, this is just horrible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这简直太糟糕了。

sentences.en: One building.
sentences.zh: 就一栋建筑。

sentences.en: There was stuff that happened.
sentences.zh: 发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: There was things stolen.
sentences.zh: 有些东西被偷了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I mean, there was paint poured on things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我的意思是，有人在东西上泼了油漆。

sentences.en: There was just lots of stuff.
sentences.zh: 总之发生了好多事。

sentences.en: Stuff here meaning?
sentences.zh: 这里说的“事”是指什么？

sentences.en: People didn't want to talk about this on tape.
sentences.zh: 人们不愿意在录音中谈论这个。

sentences.en: But I just have this mental image of a really ugly mob up in arms about this dome.
sentences.zh: 但我脑海里总有一个画面：一群群愤怒至极的暴民对这座穹顶建筑群起而攻之。

sentences.en: That's probably an exaggeration, but you get the idea.
sentences.zh: 这可能有点夸张，但你懂那个意思。

sentences.en: Despite the unrest, the dome restaurant opened in June of 1954.
sentences.zh: 尽管骚动不断，穹顶餐厅还是在1954年6月开业了。

sentences.en: And according to Joel, it was the place to go.
sentences.zh: 据乔尔说，那是当时最炙手可热的去处。

sentences.en: The dome was the most elegant place around, I mean, at that time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在那个时候，穹顶是周围最优雅的地方。

sentences.en: Certainly when you went out to eat in the 50s on Cape Cod, in a place like the dome,
sentences.zh: 当然，50年代在科德角外出吃饭时，去穹顶这样的地方，

sentences.en: you wore a tie and the women were all spiffed up.
sentences.zh: 你得系领带，女士们也都盛装打扮。

sentences.en: It was a festive occasion.
sentences.zh: 那是一个充满节日气氛的场合。

sentences.en: And they had a live musician.
sentences.zh: 他们还请了现场乐手。

sentences.en: She played the zither.
sentences.zh: 她弹奏齐特琴。

sentences.en: And I don't know if you've ever had dinner with zither music.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有一边听着齐特琴音乐一边吃过晚饭。

sentences.en: It's rather pleasant.
sentences.zh: 感觉相当惬意。

sentences.en: The restaurant is right on the ocean.
sentences.zh: 餐厅就在海边。

sentences.en: And you're far away from cities.
sentences.zh: 而且远离城市。

sentences.en: So you can just look up at the ceiling and you're looking at the stars.
sentences.zh: 所以你只要抬头看天花板，就能看到满天繁星。

sentences.en: Sally Brady was 14 years old when the dome restaurant opened near her house.
sentences.zh: 萨利·布雷迪在穹顶餐厅在她家附近开业时年仅14岁。

sentences.en: Those early 50s were really quite an amazing moment because everybody could buy cars.
sentences.zh: 50年代初确实是一个令人惊叹的时期，因为每个人都买得起汽车。

sentences.en: People who survived the war, all those men were home and there were jobs.
sentences.zh: 经历过战争幸存下来的人们，所有这些男人们都回到了家，而且有了工作。

sentences.en: And people were making the American dream come true.
sentences.zh: 人们正在让美国梦变成现实。

sentences.en: And I think that the dome was sort of a symbol of the American dream in a way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在某种程度上，穹顶可以说是美国梦的象征。

sentences.en: It felt like a prosperous, optimistic time.
sentences.zh: 那感觉是一个繁荣、乐观的时代。

sentences.en: It made sense that the dome represented the future for some people.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，穹顶代表着未来是合情合理的。

sentences.en: It turned out that there were some real structural problems with the dome.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这座穹顶存在一些真正的结构性问题。

sentences.en: First, the structure acted like an acoustic amplifier.
sentences.zh: 首先，这种结构就像一个声学扩音器。

sentences.en: So all that zither music got blasted across the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 所以所有的齐特琴音乐都被放大并传遍了整个社区。

sentences.en: And a building with that much glass worked like a greenhouse.
sentences.zh: 而且拥有这么多玻璃的建筑就像一个温室。

sentences.en: So it got hot inside.
sentences.zh: 所以里面变得很热。

sentences.en: After the first season, they covered the dome in white fiberglass to block out the sun.
sentences.zh: 在第一个营业季之后，他们在穹顶上覆盖了一层白色的玻璃纤维来阻挡阳光。

sentences.en: That meant diners couldn't see the stars anymore.
sentences.zh: 这意味着食客们再也看不到星星了。

sentences.en: Geodesic domes don't have any support beaMs.
sentences.zh: 测地穹顶没有任何支撑梁。

sentences.en: Those triangular window frames do all the work.
sentences.zh: 那些三角形的窗框承担了所有的重量。

sentences.en: Each frame rests on the one next to it.
sentences.zh: 每个窗框都靠旁边的窗框支撑。

sentences.en: Which can be a problem if the building materials are flexible and move in the wind.
sentences.zh: 如果建筑材料具有柔韧性且会在风中晃动，这可能会成为一个问题。

sentences.en: Here's Arnie Grepstad.
sentences.zh: 这位是阿尔尼·格雷普斯塔德。

sentences.en: He worked at the restaurants.
sentences.zh: 他曾在这些餐厅工作过。

sentences.en: Saturday night, horrible weather outside.
sentences.zh: 星期六晚上，外面天气糟糕透了。

sentences.en: And this particular night, there was a patio for the Scallies and that where they're having dinner.
sentences.zh: 就在那一晚，有个露台是留给“斯卡利斯”他们那群人吃晚饭的。

sentences.en: And they were regular customers, local people.
sentences.zh: 他们是老主顾，也就是当地人。

sentences.en: Around 7.30, with a chock full restaurant, all of a sudden it started dripping at table 113.
sentences.zh: 大约七点半，餐厅里座无虚席，113号桌突然开始漏水。

sentences.en: And I can remember it, seeing them sit there.
sentences.zh: 我至今还记得，看着他们坐在那里的情景。

sentences.en: And Jane took her umbrella out, opened it to a huge applause from everyone in the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 简拿出了她的雨伞，撑了开来，赢得了餐厅里所有人的热烈掌声。

sentences.en: It was just funny.
sentences.zh: 这实在太搞笑了。

sentences.en: But the fact is that geodesic domes, most of them look like sieves.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，测地穹顶，大部分看起来都像筛子一样。

sentences.en: Again, Jay Baldwin, Bucky's former student.
sentences.zh: 再次有请杰伊·鲍德温，巴基的前学生。

sentences.en: I have a photograph of Bucky inside his dome in Carbondale, with an umbrella in one hand, a book in the other, and a flashlight in his mouth, reading the book.
sentences.zh: 我有一张照片，是巴基在卡本代尔的穹顶里，一手拿伞，一手拿书，嘴里咬着手电筒在看书。

sentences.en: And the umbrella is needed.
sentences.zh: 而且确实非打伞不可。

sentences.en: I told Bucky, I'm going to find out why domes leak.
sentences.zh: 我告诉巴基，我要找出穹顶漏水的原因。

sentences.en: And he said, domes leak because they're made by amateurs and they built it with holes in it.
sentences.zh: 他说，穹顶漏水是因为它们是业余爱好者建造的，而且建的时候就带着洞。

sentences.en: You wouldn't build a boat with holes in it, would you?
sentences.zh: 你不会造一艘带洞的船吧？

sentences.en: And I said, I don't think they're leaking because they made them with a hole in it.
sentences.zh: 我说，我觉得它们漏水不是因为建造时留了洞。

sentences.en: I said, I think they're leaking geodesicly.
sentences.zh: 我说，我觉得它们是以测地线的方式在漏水。

sentences.en: The owner, Joel Peterson, says he patched a lot of leaks.
sentences.zh: 业主乔尔·彼得森说他修补了许多漏水处。

sentences.en: Eventually, Joel wanted to retire from the restaurant business.
sentences.zh: 后来，乔尔想要从餐饮业退休。

sentences.en: He sold the property in 2002.
sentences.zh: 他在2002年卖掉了这处房产。

sentences.en: It's been sitting vacant ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后它就一直闲置着。

sentences.en: I asked Joel and Arnie to give me a tour.
sentences.zh: 我请乔尔和阿尔尼带我参观一下。

sentences.en: I can't bring myself to tell them I've actually been here before.
sentences.zh: 我实在说不出口其实我以前来过这里。

sentences.en: We have to push aside branches to get to the front door.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不拨开树枝才能走到前门。

sentences.en: It's been a few years since I've been here.
sentences.zh: 我已经有好几年没来这里了。

sentences.en: And to tell you the truth, I never really wanted to come because, I mean, it is incredibly overgrown.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我其实从来不想来，因为，我的这里杂草丛生得难以想象。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just set.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就这么荒废着。

sentences.en: Oh, gosh, this is awful.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh, isn't this amazing?
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，这难道不是很神奇吗？

sentences.en: It actually, I actually have a key.
sentences.zh: 其实，我其实有一把钥匙。

sentences.en: Yo, we did.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们做到了。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what, this is not a pretty sight.
sentences.zh: 跟你直说吧，这地方真是不怎么好看。

sentences.en: I told you about Ruth welcoming the zither.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说过露丝弹着筝欢迎大家的事。

sentences.en: This is where she played.
sentences.zh: 这就是她以前演奏的地方。

sentences.en: Now, you want to take a look at the kitchen?
sentences.zh: 现在，你想去看看厨房吗？

sentences.en: There's a walk-in cooler there and the prep room in the back.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个步入式冷藏库，后面是准备间。

sentences.en: This really has been my work in life.
sentences.zh: 这真的是我一生的心血。

sentences.en: Certainly, I wouldn't mind seeing it restored.
sentences.zh: 当然，我不会介意看到它恢复原貌。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I think it's going to be a tremendous expense to put this back.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我觉得把这东西修好要花一大笔钱。

sentences.en: So it's with two opposite emotions that you look at it.
sentences.zh: 所以你看着它的时候会有两种截然相反的情绪。

sentences.en: But you have to be realistic and understand that things change here in life.
sentences.zh: 但你必须现实一点，明白生活中的事物是会变的。

sentences.en: In 2006, a real estate development company planned to build condos on the side.
sentences.zh: 在2006年，一家房地产开发公司计划在旁边建造公寓。

sentences.en: And for a while, it looked like the dome might be torn down.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，这个穹顶看起来甚至可能会被拆掉。

sentences.en: But then a funny thing happened.
sentences.zh: 但随后发生了一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: There was a public outcry to keep the dome.
sentences.zh: 公众发出强烈呼吁，要求保留这个穹顶。

sentences.en: This is the same building that residents fought against tooth and nail
sentences.zh: 这就是当年居民们曾拼命反对的同一栋建筑

sentences.en: back when it was being constructed in the 50s.
sentences.zh: 早在50年代它建造的时候。

sentences.en: Now, in order to build on the site, the developer has to restore the dome.
sentences.zh: 现在，为了在这个地方进行开发，开发商必须修复穹顶。

sentences.en: And that's going to be expensive.
sentences.zh: 而那可是一笔不小的开销。

sentences.en: So the whole thing is in limbo until more condos are pre-sold.
sentences.zh: 所以整件事现在处于悬而未决的状态，直到有更多公寓预售出去。

sentences.en: And real estate transactions are not moving quickly these days.
sentences.zh: 而且如今的房地产交易并不景气。

sentences.en: If the developer can't pre-sell enough condos to justify the cost of restoring the dome,
sentences.zh: 如果开发商无法预售足够多的公寓来抵消修复穹顶的成本，

sentences.en: then the whole deal could fall apart.
sentences.zh: 那么整桩交易可能会泡汤。

sentences.en: If that happened, the dome would stay as it is now, continuing to decay,
sentences.zh: 如果发生那种情况，穹顶就会保持现状，继续荒废下去，

sentences.en: waiting for the next out-of-towners to come poking around with a flashlight.
sentences.zh: 等待着下一拨外地人拿着手电筒来这里东翻西找。

sentences.en: The person who seems least sentimental about this is Joel Peterson.
sentences.zh: 对这件事表现得最不感伤的人是乔尔·彼得森。

sentences.en: If I were doing the project that they talk about doing, I'd tear it down.
sentences.zh: 如果让我来做他们说的那种项目，我早就把它拆了。

sentences.en: To be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实跟你说吧。

sentences.en: It's a building.
sentences.zh: 它就是个建筑。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was part of my life.
sentences.zh: 对，它曾是我生活的一部分。

sentences.en: It's a building.
sentences.zh: 但它也就是个建筑。

sentences.en: Sally Brady, who grew up next to the dome, feels differently.
sentences.zh: 在穹顶旁边长大的莎莉·布雷迪则有不同的感受。

sentences.en: Maybe it will be reborn in a different way that will be better.
sentences.zh: 也许它会以一种更好、不同的方式重获新生。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Maybe it will be a beautiful, transparent place,
sentences.zh: 也许它会成为一个美丽、通透的地方，

sentences.en: and people will go there and do fantastic, energizing work that will help humanity.
sentences.zh: 人们会去那里从事充满奇思妙想、振奋人心的工作，为人类造福。

sentences.en: What do you think we would lose if it was torn down?
sentences.zh: 你觉得如果它被拆了，我们会失去什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's a very good example of anything was possible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是“皆有可能”的一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah, I sort of agree.
sentences.zh: 对，我有点同感。

sentences.en: And then what does it mean that now it's just in such disrepair?
sentences.zh: 那么现在它变得如此破败，又意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think it means that we've moved on, and that dream went bust, sort of.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这意味着我们已经向前看了，而且那个梦想可以说是破灭了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's a kind of broken dream right now.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得现在它就像是一个破碎的梦想。

sentences.en: It's sort of depressing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点沮丧，不是吗？

sentences.en: Maybe a finished dream is a little kinder.
sentences.zh: 也许一个画上句号的梦想会温柔一点。

sentences.en: Buckminster Fuller claimed that his ideas were 50 years ahead of his time.
sentences.zh: 巴克明斯特·富勒曾声称他的理念领先了他所处的时代50年。

sentences.en: And now it's been over 50 years, but domes have not replaced traditional buildings.
sentences.zh: 现在已经过去50多年了，但穹顶并没有取代传统建筑。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm rooting for the dome.
sentences.zh: 我还是支持穹顶的。

sentences.en: I think it represents Bucky's optimism that we could solve the world's problems with good design.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它代表了巴基的乐观精神，即我们可以用优秀的设计来解决世界上的问题。

sentences.en: And even if you couldn't, you could still stargaze through triangular windows,
sentences.zh: 而且就算你解决不了，你仍然可以透过三角形的窗户看星星，

sentences.en: looking out over the sea.
sentences.zh: 眺望远方的海景。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Katie Cloxon with Sam Greenspan and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》由凯蒂·克洛克森与山姆·格林斯潘以及我——罗曼·马斯共同制作。

sentences.en: Katie produced a different version of this story at the Transom Story Workshop,
sentences.zh: 凯蒂在特兰索姆故事工作坊制作了这期节目的不同版本，

sentences.en: which aired on the PRX Howe Sound podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 该节目曾在PRX的豪湾播客上播出。

sentences.en: Both of those are run by the great, super punk rock, Rob Rosenthal.
sentences.zh: 这两档节目都由那位伟大的、超级朋克摇滚的罗伯·罗森塔尔运营。

sentences.en: Do they owe us a living?
sentences.zh: 他们欠我们生计吗？

sentences.en: Thanks also to Aaron Krzyzewski.
sentences.zh: 同时感谢阿伦·科日谢夫斯基。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都开通了Twitter、Instagram和Spotify账号。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links,
sentences.zh: 但要想了解关于这个故事的更多信息，包括酷炫的图片和链接，

sentences.en: and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 并收听《99%无形》的所有单集，你必须访问 99pi.org。
